correctness.rationale: For all integers d>=4, direct differentiation proves smoothness. Every line has rank-one/rank-two coordinate-pair projections; rank-two on both sides would identify root sets of u^d+uv^(d-1) and z^d-w^d, which is impossible because one root set is not concyclic and the other is. This exhausts d^2 lines. Adjunction gives normal bundle O(2-d) and therefore a reduced finite Fano scheme. The row/column intersection rule and explicit Kronecker-product eigenvectors give the line-class matrix spectrum; hyperplane-class containment and Hodge index turn its rank into exactly the dimension of the line-class span. A packaged exact-arithmetic checker executed successfully for d=4,5,6. Finite computation is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source selects this specific arithmetic sextic double solid because its branch curves enable potential density. A complete finite-etale description of its branch-surface line Hilbert scheme identifies every possible line input over Q and over C, and determines its entire line-intersection configuration and a rank-26 subspace of its geometric Neron--Severi group. The result is a complete natural classification and extends uniformly to all degrees d>=4, with a sharp boundary at d=3, not an arbitrary numerological slice. It does not purport to compute the full Picard number.
